first_principle: Debt is a dated promise to move future cash to someone else.
plain_question: Did the company improve its future cash position, or only move the payment date?
core_mechanism: A company raises new money, pays off or changes old obligations, changes interest cost or maturity, and then must support the new promise with future operating cash.
company_examples: PBF; Devon; Matador; Liberty Broadband; Verizon; Wheaton
proof_needed: new debt terms; old debt payoff; fees; taxes; coupon change; maturity change; liquidity; covenant cushion; cash-flow coverage; NPV

first_principle: Buying scale is not the same as earning from scale.
plain_question: What was bought, how was it funded, and did the acquired base convert into cash?
core_mechanism: Money buys a company, customer base, backlog, route, asset, or capability. The deal only works if the acquired thing produces revenue, margin, collections, and debt-service capacity after close.
company_examples: Core & Main; Sherwin-Williams; Lowe's; URI/Yak; Sterling; MasTec; Relation; MAI
proof_needed: purchase price; cash/debt/equity mix; acquired revenue; acquired backlog; purchase accounting; integration costs; margin; working capital; collections
common_bad_claim: A larger company is automatically a better company.

first_principle: A loan is safer only if the pledged asset can turn into cash when needed.
plain_question: What asset backs the borrowing, and can it actually be collected, sold, rented, or financed?
core_mechanism: Receivables, inventory, fleet, leases, card loans, or equipment become borrowing support. The key is eligibility, advance rate, loss risk, and cash conversion.
company_examples: United Rentals; Target; Zebra; Pool; MSC Industrial; Global Industrial; Synchrony; Arrow
proof_needed: borrowing base; eligible collateral; receivable aging; inventory turns; advance rates; charge-offs; reserves; trustee reports; collections
common_bad_claim: Balance-sheet assets automatically equal borrowing quality.

first_principle: A plan matters only when money becomes usable capacity.
plain_question: Can capital spending become productive assets, output, and cash?
core_mechanism: A company spends money on plants, equipment, infrastructure, projects, or fleet. The spend matters if the asset enters service, produces output, and earns enough cash after maintenance, financing, and time.
company_examples: Jacobs; Steel Dynamics; Eaton; Energy Transfer; Cheniere; Nucor; AECOM; Knife River; KBR; United Rentals
proof_needed: capex; project status; in-service date; output; utilization; contract duration; revenue; OCF; debt service; maintenance capex; return model
common_bad_claim: Capex automatically means growth or return.

first_principle: Public demand becomes company revenue only through authority, budget, contract, and collection.
plain_question: Which public body approved the spending, and who is obligated to pay?
core_mechanism: Government, utility, defense, transportation, water, or infrastructure need becomes a funded contract, rate recovery, grant, or approved capital plan. The proof is the legal funding path, not the social need.
company_examples: CACI; Leidos; Granite; AECOM; utilities; public contractors
proof_needed: appropriation; order; grant; rate case; tariff; contract award; funded backlog; billing; collection; change-order risk
common_bad_claim: Public need automatically becomes funded company revenue.

first_principle: Water systems fail slowly, but repair cannot be ignored forever.
plain_question: Who supplies and finances the repair of pipes, drainage, treatment, fire protection, and utility systems?
core_mechanism: Aging public and private systems require replacement parts, pipe, valves, meters, engineering, construction, and regulated or municipal funding. The channel is local, physical, and permission-heavy.
company_examples: Core & Main; Ferguson; American Water Works; Granite; AECOM
proof_needed: municipal budgets; rate base; project awards; pipe and waterworks sales; backlog; branch economics; receivables; collections
common_bad_claim: Water scarcity or aging infrastructure automatically makes every supplier a winner.

first_principle: Energy value depends on moving molecules from where they are produced to where they are used or exported.
plain_question: Which route, terminal, pipe, plant, or contract turns volume into cash?
core_mechanism: Pipelines, fractionators, storage, export terminals, LNG trains, and processing plants earn only when volumes move through assets under tariffs, contracts, spreads, or fees.
company_examples: ONEOK; Plains; Targa; Energy Transfer; Williams; Cheniere
proof_needed: route; tariff; contract; volume; utilization; capex; debt; DCF; EBITDA; project contribution; shipper/customer support
common_bad_claim: A pipeline network automatically earns more because energy demand exists.

first_principle: Electricity cannot scale without physical gear.
plain_question: Who supplies the equipment that lets power be generated, switched, protected, measured, and delivered?
core_mechanism: Grid, data-center, industrial, and utility demand needs turbines, switchgear, transformers, cable, controls, power-quality systems, sensors, and service capacity. The bottleneck is physical delivery, not only demand.
company_examples: Eaton; Teledyne; electrical distributors; turbine suppliers; WESCO
proof_needed: orders; backlog; capacity; lead times; customer deposits; delivery schedule; revenue recognition; margin; working capital
common_bad_claim: Demand for electrification automatically proves supplier cash flow.

first_principle: An investment is different from cash in hand.
plain_question: How do investors get liquidity when assets stay private?
core_mechanism: Private funds, continuation vehicles, secondaries, tender offers, semi-liquid funds, and redemption queues create ways to transfer ownership or return cash without selling assets publicly.
company_examples: Blackstone; KKR; Apollo; Carlyle/AlpInvest; Ares; BlackRock
proof_needed: subscription terms; redemption terms; tender documents; secondary sale price; distributions; fees; NAV; DPI; TVPI; IRR
common_bad_claim: Private-market AUM automatically means investors can get cash when they want.

first_principle: A new lender does not prove the old lender disappeared.
plain_question: Who actually supplied the credit, and did banks stay in the stack?
core_mechanism: Private credit, BDCs, banks, ABL lenders, revolvers, bonds, and agent banks can coexist. A deal may replace one bank loan while preserving bank roles elsewhere.
company_examples: Ares borrower rows; Auctane; Frontline; PBF; Matador; URI
proof_needed: credit agreement; lender list; admin agent; revolver banks; payoff language; facility size; collateral; pricing; treasury or hedging role
common_bad_claim: Private credit has replaced banks everywhere.
